title: Apraxia Post-Stroke Affolter Rehabilitations-Trial
summary:
Apraxia is a disorder in which people have difficulty performing specific, learned movements—even though their muscles are strong enough, their senses are functioning normally, and they want to understand the task. It is therefore not a form of paralysis or a sensory problem, but rather a disruption of “movement planning” in the brain. This makes everyday activities that require the use of the arms and hands (e.g., getting dressed, preparing meals) particularly difficult.

The planned study will examine whether a specific rehabilitation intervention—the Affolter Model® over at least six weeks—leads to different improvements in daily living independence for people with apraxia following a stroke compared to standard, guideline-based rehabilitation (e.g., ADL strategy training, gesture imitation, arm function training, and robotics).

interventions.name:
75 minutes Affolter Model®-Therapy per weekday (physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech therapy) combined in combination with an Affolter Model®-based nursing concept (45 minutes on each calendar day). The intervention is delivered as part of routine inpatient rehabilitation care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
(i) Legal age and consent to participate in the study (patients with or without capacity to provide informed consent may be included; if consent was obtained by a legal representative, the patient’s own consent must be obtained as soon as possible),
(ii) inpatient treatment in phase B or C, early- or neurorehabilitation in Switzerland, respectively
(iii) stroke (ICD-10 codes: I61, I63), left-hemispheric or right-hemispheric with apraxia [defined according to KAS cut-off ≤ 76 points (left-hemispheric) or ≤ 46 in KAS-R points (right-hemispheric), respectively], onset of acute stroke 2–12 weeks prior to inclusion,
(iv) patients are awake and contactable, defined as GCS ≥ 10 points with the following minimum subscale scores:
• Eye Opening (E): ≥4
• Verbal Response (V): ≥1
• Motor Response (M): ≥5
Exclusion criteria:
(i) Life expectancy < 12 months according to medical assessment,
(ii) advised by qualified personnel that the individual is not eligible (for example, due to a visa restriction that prevents the tests from being administered)
(iii) insufficient German language skills for endpoints for patient OR representative,
(iv) pre-existing dementia/neurodegenerative disease (anamnestically),
(v) previous stroke or other brain damage,
(vi) residential distance > 150 km from study centre,
(vii) Participation in another ongoing clinical trial (except follow-up time)
(viii) serious, clinically significant psychiatric disorder.
